q: All carbon-containing compounds derived from living organisms are called:
All carbon compounds obtained from living tissue are called biomolecules.
The reagent used to grind living tissue into a slurry for fractionation is:
Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) is used to obtain the slurry.

The molecular weight cut-off between biomicromolecules and biomacromolecules is approximately:
Molecules under 1000 Da are micromolecules; over 1000 Da are macromolecules.

Which element shows the greatest relative enrichment in the human body compared to the earth's crust?
Carbon rises from 0.03% (crust) to 18.5% (human body) — the sharpest relative enrichment.
Which of these is an example of an inorganic constituent of living tissue?
CaCO3 is a listed inorganic constituent; the others are organic biomicromolecules.

Lipids are found in the acid-insoluble fraction mainly because they are:

Which analysis method is used specifically to detect inorganic elements like Ca, Mg, S, P in a tissue?
Drying then burning the tissue to ash reveals its inorganic constituents.

Starch is made of alpha-glucose units.

Cellulose glucose units are joined by beta-1,4-glycosidic bonds.
The glycosidic linkage joining glucose units in starch is:
Starch glucose units are joined by alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds.
Which polysaccharide is the storage polysaccharide of animals, also called 'animal starch'?
Glycogen is the animal storage polysaccharide.

Heteropolysaccharides involve amino sugars and chemically modified sugars.
Exoskeletons of arthropods & fungal cell walls
Chitin forms the arthropod exoskeleton and fungal cell wall.

Proteins, along with nucleic acids and polysaccharides, are acid-insoluble biomacromolecules.

Uracil occurs in RNA in place of DNA's thymine.
DNA typically exists as a double helix (double-stranded).
Which bases are common to both DNA and RNA?
Adenine, guanine and cytosine occur in both DNA and RNA.
The bond linking successive nucleotides in a polynucleotide chain is a:
A phosphodiester bond links the sugar of one nucleotide to the phosphate of the next.
The bond linking a nitrogenous base to its sugar (within one nucleotide) is a/an:
An N-glycosidic bond attaches the base to the sugar.

Deoxyribose lacks the 2'-OH group present in ribose.
Proteins are built from amino acid monomers.
The bond linking amino acids in a protein chain is called a:
Amino acids are linked by peptide bonds.
Proteins are called heteropolymers because they are made of:

The polypeptide chain contains many different amino acid types.
The most abundant protein in the human body is:
Collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body.
The most abundant protein in the biosphere is:
RuBisCO is the most abundant protein across the entire biosphere.
The first amino acid of a polypeptide chain is called the:
The first amino acid is the N-terminal amino acid.

The protein becomes biologically active once it reaches its tertiary (3-D folded) structure.

Amino acids are primary metabolites, directly involved in growth/development/reproduction.
Which of these is a secondary metabolite?

Nearly all enzymes are proteins (ribozymes being the exception).
The nucleic-acid-based exception to 'enzymes are proteins' is called a:
Ribozymes are RNA molecules that act as enzymes.
The pocket/crevice in an enzyme where the substrate binds is called the:
The active site is where the substrate binds and catalysis occurs.
The protein portion of an enzyme (without its cofactor) is called the:
The apoenzyme is the protein-only part of the enzyme.
A catalytically active enzyme (apoenzyme + cofactor together) is called a:

Low temperature affects an enzyme by:

Low temperature reversibly inactivates the enzyme without destroying it.
The maximum velocity of an enzymatic reaction, once the enzyme is saturated with substrate, is called:
Vmax is the maximum reaction velocity.
The Michaelis–Menten constant (Km) is defined as the substrate concentration at:
Km = [S] at half the maximum velocity.
Why does reaction velocity plateau at Vmax even with more substrate added?
All enzyme active sites are saturated
At Vmax, enzyme molecules are saturated with substrate; no free enzyme remains to bind more.

The relative abundance of carbon and hydrogen
The presence of nitrogen only in living tissue
